beta_new: Head up and leftward, clipping three bolts (Revelation shares the third), then from there trend up and rightward to a stance for the belay. Next go straight up and then rightward again to the following belay; three pitches in all.
Climb the biggest slab; the only bolt comes high up.
Clip the opening bolt from a stick. The boulder-problem crux sits right at the base; once past it you step onto terrain that is less steep.
Climb a crack system that goes straight up beside a cave; a single bolt sits roughly thirty feet off the ground.
Begin fifteen feet beyond Jedi Master, then climb a crack that trends up-left beside a little bush, moving onto the face to clip a single bolt.
Pull through the crimps to the second bolt, work the thin reachy sequence above it, then continue to the top.
Eight bolts lead up the northwest arete above the water. The loose rock on the line's right has largely gone over the years.
Follow the right-hand bolt line; how hard it feels depends on how closely you stay with the bolts.
Four bolts protect it.

moves.from: a few small pieces of gear are worth carrying

value.text: A few small pieces of gear.

beta_new: Five bolts lead to the shared anchors, though clip one can easily be skipped.
Three bolts lead up the north face; after the third, trend leftward and upward to join a neighboring route at its lone bolt.

moves.from: A rappel anchor partway up the line means a single rope is enough to get down.

beta_new: Pull through the undercut on its leftmost edge to a bolt, then angle rightward for the next bolt, which sits at the shoulder; keep going to the top. The first clip is a long reach and the start holds the crux; a variation starting beyond the undercut's leftmost end is slightly easier.
A bold lead that pulls over the undercut near its right-hand end, with two bolts along the way.
Begin beneath a chockstone and work the cracks leftward, clipping a couple of bolts close to the top.
Fun, pocketed climbing, with one slightly committing stretch in the gap separating bolts three and four.
Step off the round boulder, clip the lone bolt, and complete the climb in the leftward-leaning groove.

moves.from: gear up to about 6 inches is useful

beta_new: Pitch one scoots over a short apron, clipping a trio of bolts plus a pin hammered into a flake, to a ledge beneath a long arching corner system. Above, a string of bolts forms a ladder that looks never to have been completed.

Begin behind a boulder and take the leftmost fissure, trending leftward to Bat Ledge. Pitch two drifts leftward, nearly brushing a neighboring line, then returns rightward to meet another route where it has a bolt.

Follow the crack that slants rightward to the far end of a shelf, shuffle over, work a hairline fissure upward, and bear rightward for the exit. The original line instead leaves the left-hand ledge past a bolt and angles right to join the main way.
Enter a corner that faces left, traverse leftward under a roof to reach a shelf, then keep going on the wall overhead, clipping two bolts.
Bouldery, awkward climbing; the final three bolts are common to a neighboring route.
Step onto a dike that slants leftward, climb leftward, then head directly upward, clipping a bolt on the way to a crack. A direct start further left is harder.
Three bolts protect the diagonal ledge as it climbs toward the left.
Think about gear placements carefully between the two bolts, and extend your clips, since drag builds up.
A thin crack leads up toward a single bolt high on the route.
A slim crack leads to a ledge; cross a neighboring route there and carry on up the crack above, which soon takes hand-sized gear.
Start from the right edge of the rightmost cave and climb out over its lip, using plentiful huecos and pockets. A slabby stretch follows, then a roof just under the anchors holds the crux.
Cams can protect the roof moves that gain the initial clip, so bring a few.

moves.from: Cams can protect the roof moves that gain the initial clip, so bring a few.

value.text: A few cams for the roof moves.

beta_new: Pre-clip the opening bolt with a stick, or climb a neighboring route and clip it during the descent. The hard, bouldery sequence comes immediately off the ground.

Pitch one follows an inside corner, then trends rightward to a short, strenuous lieback onto Log Ledge. Pitch two begins with a very hard move past a bolt, eases for a stretch, then traverses rightward to a protruding knob and then three further bolts to a crescent-shaped dihedral, which you abandon to the right at the earliest chance.

Big holds next to a crack lead to a friction move trending left. Higher, a bolt guards a run of friction moves over a crystalline ridge, then a gentle lieback crack and a leftward traverse reach the foot of a trough, which has solid holds all the way to the summit.
Work up and right along a ramp until partway along it, then continue vertically with a series of mantles, passing a bolt.
The difficulty is packed into the opening moves: very cruxy climbing from the ground to just beyond the second bolt.
Begin on the neighboring route, then move up and rightward through a hole and on past a few bolts. The moves can be easier or harder depending on your height.
Aim for the center of the trail-side wall, clipping a pair of bolts and a tree that is already slung.
Climb the wall to the right of Billabong's middle stretch, clip a bolt, enter a crack, and join Billabong where its plated pillar begins.
Climb to a piton, then follow a dike that traverses rightward past an old rurp and a pair of bolts before finishing up a slender fissure.
Once past bolt number two, drift leftward and top out close to where the neighboring crack ends.
Pick whichever of the two crack systems appeals at the start; higher up, three bolts protect the way. Starting by the right-hand option, you may want to split the route into two pitches.
